19	# CSR transport bring-up for a new Andes core
20	
21	Inputs you need from the user (ask if missing):
22	- The AndeStar V5 SPA PDF for the core family (the repo carries
23	  `AndeStar_V5_SPA_UM164_V1.7.pdf` for the current cores).
24	- The engine name (e.g. `ax45mpv_premium`) and a built vsim checkout
25	  (`VSIM_BIN_DIR` in `config.env` points at its `build/`).
26	- Optionally the matching QEMU `-cpu` name for the oracle leg.
27	
28	The goal: every CSR the core implements and the ROI can touch is restored at
29	resume, re-read at drain, and `--verify`-compared -- and every CSR the core
30	does NOT implement is gated off, because the batched Program-Buffer sweep
31	faults (cmderr=3) on a single over-claimed CSR.
32	
33	Work in this order. Each phase has a reference file with the details --
34	read it when you reach the phase, not before.
35	
36	## Phase 0: establish ground truth
37	
38	The engine's compiled-in config is the ONLY truth about what it implements.
39	Read `$VSIM_BIN_DIR/V<engine>/obj_sc/config.inc` (the BUILD directory copy --
40	the `external/` source tree can differ from what was actually built) and
41	`sim_<engine> --describe`. Do not trust QEMU: its gdbstub exposes CSRs the
42	vsim RTL does not implement (QEMU models a fuller core), and restoring or
43	sweeping one of those stalls or faults the Debug Module.
44	
45	## Phase 1: mine the spec
46	
47	Run `scripts/extract_csr_inventory.py <spec.pdf>` to refresh
48	`tests/andes_csr/csr_inventory.csv` (needs PyMuPDF; use a venv). Then pull,
49	for each CSR the core claims: the IM Requirement (existence condition), the
50	Access Mode, and the reset value. The SPA has a fixed per-CSR layout and a
51	consolidated existence table (Table 13) -- see
52	`references/spec-mining.md` for the exact headers and extraction recipes.
53	
54	## Phase 2: classify dispositions
55	
56	Run `scripts/classify_csr_coverage.py tests/andes_csr/csr_inventory.csv` and
57	the guard `tests/andes_csr/check_coverage.py`. The guard enforces
58	inventory == matrix == ABI (`include/hybrid/state_abi.h`), so a CSR added to
59	the wire format without a disposition (or vice versa) fails loudly. New
60	transported CSRs are one X-macro line in `state_abi.h`
61	(`HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST` / `HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST`); every consumer
62	(plugin drain, restore, drain re-read, verify) iterates the same list.
63	
64	## Phase 3: bind capability gates
65	
66	For each transported CSR, map its IM Requirement to a gate in the vsim
67	repo's `src/hybrid/andes_caps.hpp` (address -> gate) and bind the gate to a
68	`_NDS_*` config macro in `andes_caps_config.hpp` (absent macro reads as
69	"off" -- never a compile error). The gate must encode the SPEC's existence
70	condition, not a plausibly-related feature; two real bugs came from getting
71	this wrong. Follow TDD: model the new engine's config shape as a caps
72	helper in `tests/hybrid/andes_caps.test.cpp` and write the failing
73	expectation first. Read `references/caps-gating.md` -- it carries the
74	hard-won rules and the write-prerequisite (setup ordering) requirements.
75	
76	## Phase 4: reset values and verify exclusions
77	
78	Two reset-value sources exist and they legitimately differ:
79	- The SPA reset table (documentation; many fields are IM = implementation
80	  determined or DC = don't care).
81	- The EMPIRICAL baseline the simulator drains from the freshly reset hart
82	  (cached per engine build + ELF). The liveness gate compares against this
83	  one -- it is self-truthing, so spec IM/DC values need no manual table.
84	
85	Where QEMU's reset differs from the engine's reset for a CSR the program
86	never writes (e.g. `msp_bound`, `milmb` enable bit), a strict compare
87	false-positives: add it to `andes_verify_excluded` in
88	`driver/state_diff.cpp` with a comment naming the divergence. Do NOT
89	exclude a CSR to hide a transport bug -- exclusion is only for
90	engine-implementation artifacts.
91	
92	## Phase 5: validate (the ladder)
93	
94	Run bottom-up; each rung catches what the one below cannot. The key
95	insight: the tolerant abstract path MASKS capability bugs (a faulting read
96	mirrors as zero, QEMU drains zero too, --verify falsely matches), so only
97	the batched CSR sweep truly validates the caps table -- it faults on an
98	over-claim and bisects to NAME the offending CSR. A cold-cache hybrid run
99	exercises it via the baseline capture. Full commands, expected outputs, and
100	failure playbook: `references/validation.md`.
101	
102	## Phase 6: register the engine (per-engine test completeness)
103	
104	andesim is a commercial product: every supported engine BUILD must ship its
105	own complete, machine-checked CSR test artifacts -- and a rebuild of the
106	same core with a different config counts as a NEW registration (the
107	config.inc hash is the identity, so reuse is impossible by construction).
108	Four deliverables per engine build: the CSR manifest (every spec CSR:

110	completeness check (over-claims fault the sweep; under-claims -- implemented

112	a human's memory), generated per-engine write-survival fixtures, and a
113	registration guard so an unregistered engine fails loudly. Read
114	`references/engine-registration.md` for the contract, the file layout, and
115	the recipes (including what to build the first time the tooling is missing).
116

118	
119	TDD and Tidy First apply: caps fixes, sweep/transport changes, and docs are

2	
3	## Extract text once, grep many times
4	
5	```sh
6	python -m venv /tmp/pdfvenv && /tmp/pdfvenv/bin/pip -q install pymupdf
7	/tmp/pdfvenv/bin/python - <<'EOF'
8	import fitz, sys
9	doc = fitz.open("AndeStar_V5_SPA_UM164_V1.7.pdf")
10	with open("/tmp/spa.txt", "w") as f:
11	    for i, page in enumerate(doc, 1):
12	        f.write(f"===PAGE {i}===\n" + page.get_text())
13	EOF
14	```
15	
16	The repo already automates the inventory step:
17	`scripts/extract_csr_inventory.py <spec.pdf> [out.csv]` writes
18	`tests/andes_csr/csr_inventory.csv` (addr, privilege, name, mode, section).
19	Run it when the spec revision changes; the committed CSV is the checked-in
20	truth the coverage guard reads.
21	
22	## Per-CSR section layout (chapters 8-10)
23	
24	Every CSR gets a section with fixed headers -- grep for the mnemonic, then
25	read the block:
26	
27	```
28	8.3.8
29	User Scratch Register
30	Mnemonic Name: uscratch
31	IM Requirement: misa[13]==1 (N extension)     <- existence condition
32	Access Mode: User                              <- privilege mode
33	CSR Address: 0x040 (standard read/write)
34	XLEN: 64 and 32
35	<bit-field diagram: per-field name, type (RW/RO/W1C/...), reset value>
36	```
37	
38	- `IM Requirement:` is THE existence condition. This is what the caps gate
39	  must encode (Phase 3). "Always" means gate ALWAYS.
40	- `Access Mode:` gives the privilege mode the user asked about ("which mode
41	  supports this CSR"): Machine / Supervisor / User / Debug.
42	- Field types use the terminology page (chapter 9.1): IM = implementation
43	  determined, DC = reset value is don't care, RO/WO/RW/W1C/WS/RAZWI.
44	  IM and DC reset values CANNOT be tabled from the spec -- that is exactly
45	  why the empirical reset baseline (Phase 4) is the source the liveness
46	  gate uses.
47	
48	## Table 13: the consolidated existence table
49	
50	"Table 13: Existence configuration condition(s)" lists CSR groups against
51	their conditions in one place -- faster than walking every section, and the
52	authoritative cross-check when a per-section IM Requirement reads
53	ambiguously. Real rows:
54	
55	```
56	mcounterinten                 mmsc_cfg.PMNDS==1
57	mcounterwen                   (mmsc_cfg.PMNDS==1) & (misa[20]==1) // user
58	mcountermask_m
59	mcountermask_u
60	mcounterovf
61	mcountermask_s                (mmsc_cfg.PMNDS==1) & (misa[18]==1) // supervisor
62	mcounteren                    misa[20]==1 // user mode

# Mining the AndeStar V5 SPA PDF

## Extract text once, grep many times

```sh
python -m venv /tmp/pdfvenv && /tmp/pdfvenv/bin/pip -q install pymupdf
/tmp/pdfvenv/bin/python - <<'EOF'
import fitz, sys
doc = fitz.open("AndeStar_V5_SPA_UM164_V1.7.pdf")
with open("/tmp/spa.txt", "w") as f:
    for i, page in enumerate(doc, 1):
        f.write(f"===PAGE {i}===\n" + page.get_text())
EOF
```

The repo already automates the inventory step:
`scripts/extract_csr_inventory.py <spec.pdf> [out.csv]` writes
`tests/andes_csr/csr_inventory.csv` (addr, privilege, name, mode, section).
Run it when the spec revision changes; the committed CSV is the checked-in
truth the coverage guard reads.

## Per-CSR section layout (chapters 8-10)

Every CSR gets a section with fixed headers -- grep for the mnemonic, then
read the block:

```
8.3.8
User Scratch Register
Mnemonic Name: uscratch
IM Requirement: misa[13]==1 (N extension)     <- existence condition
Access Mode: User                              <- privilege mode
CSR Address: 0x040 (standard read/write)
XLEN: 64 and 32
<bit-field diagram: per-field name, type (RW/RO/W1C/...), reset value>
```

- `IM Requirement:` is THE existence condition. This is what the caps gate
  must encode (Phase 3). "Always" means gate ALWAYS.
- `Access Mode:` gives the privilege mode the user asked about ("which mode
  supports this CSR"): Machine / Supervisor / User / Debug.
- Field types use the terminology page (chapter 9.1): IM = implementation
  determined, DC = reset value is don't care, RO/WO/RW/W1C/WS/RAZWI.
  IM and DC reset values CANNOT be tabled from the spec -- that is exactly
  why the empirical reset baseline (Phase 4) is the source the liveness
  gate uses.

## Table 13: the consolidated existence table

"Table 13: Existence configuration condition(s)" lists CSR groups against
their conditions in one place -- faster than walking every section, and the
authoritative cross-check when a per-section IM Requirement reads
ambiguously. Real rows:

```
mcounterinten                 mmsc_cfg.PMNDS==1
mcounterwen                   (mmsc_cfg.PMNDS==1) & (misa[20]==1) // user
mcountermask_m
mcountermask_u
mcounterovf
mcountermask_s                (mmsc_cfg.PMNDS==1) & (misa[18]==1) // supervisor
mcounteren                    misa[20]==1 // user mode
```

Note the grouping: a condition line applies to the CSR names stacked above
it (PDF table extraction flattens the rows). `misa[20]` = U-mode present,
`misa[18]` = S-mode present. Cross-map to config.inc:
`NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS >= 2` -> U-mode, `== 3` -> S-mode;
`mmsc_cfg.PMNDS` -> the Andes perf-monitor feature.

## What "supported mode" means for transport

The transport envelope is bare-metal, single-hart, trap-free ROI, M or M+U.
So:
- M-mode CSRs (`0x3xx`, `0x7xx`, `0xBxx` machine): transport candidates.
- U-mode CSRs (`0x0xx`, `0x8xx`): transported only for the M+U envelope
  (disposition NEW_UDELTA) and gated on the UMODE gate.
- S-mode / Hypervisor / Debug-mode CSRs: excluded (EXCL_MODE / EXCL_DEBUG)
  until the S/U-envelope work needs them.
See `scripts/classify_csr_coverage.py`'s docstring for the full
disposition legend.

1	// Andes-CSR capability gating.
2	//
3	// A core implements an Andes custom CSR only when the matching feature is
4	// configured into it (config.inc). Restoring a CSR the target core lacks can
5	// hang the DMI handshake -- observed on ax45mpv_premium for ucode (no DSP) and
6	// mecc_code (no ECC). So the resume/drain loops transport only the CSRs the
7	// target core supports, decided here from the core's feature gates.
8	//
9	// This header is Verilator/SystemC-free: it maps a CSR address to its gate and
10	// answers "does a core with these gates support this CSR". The binding of each
11	// gate to the core's compiled-in `_NDS_*` config macros lives in the sim binary
12	// (see andes_caps_from_config), so this stays unit-testable in isolation.
13	#ifndef ANDES_HYBRID_ANDES_CAPS_HPP
14	#define ANDES_HYBRID_ANDES_CAPS_HPP
15	
16	#include <cstdint>
17	#include <string>
18	#include <vector>
19	
20	#include "hybrid/state_abi.h"
21	
22	namespace hybrid {
23	
24	// The hardware feature that gates each transported CSR. ALWAYS = unconditionally
25	// present (a base machine CSR every core has; never gated off). The first block
26	// gates the v3 Andes custom CSRs; the second block (UMODE..TRIGGER) gates the v4
27	// M-ext CSRs (HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST) -- standard + Andes M-mode CSRs whose
28	// existence depends on a privilege level or extension the core may not have.
29	enum class AndesGate : uint8_t {
30	  ALWAYS = 0,
31	  DSP,
32	  CODENSE,
33	  ZCMT,        // standard Zcmt table jump (jvt); NOT implied by CoDense
34	  POWERBRAKE,
35	  STACKSAFE,
36	  ECC,
37	  PMA,
38	  ILM,
39	  DLM,
40	  PERF_MONITOR,
41	  // v4 M-ext gates.
42	  UMODE,       // needs U-mode  (NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS >= 2)
43	  SMODE,       // needs S-mode  (NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS == 3)
44	  EPMP,        // ePMP / Smepmp (mseccfg)
45	  SMRNMI,      // resumable NMI (mnscratch/mnepc/mncause/mnstatus/mnvec/mrnxvec)
46	  EXCSLVL,     // exception save levels (msave*)
47	  CLIC,        // CLIC / enhanced CLIC (mtvt/mintthresh/mcirq_entry)
48	  SMSTATEEN,   // state-enable (mstateen0..3)
49	  CCTL,        // cache control CSRs (mcctlbeginaddr/mcctldata)
50	  PPI,         // private peripheral interface base (mppib)
51	  FIO,         // fast IO base (mfiob)
52	  TRIGGER,     // debug triggers (tselect/tdata1/tdata2/tcontrol/mcontext)
53	};
54	
55	// Map an Andes CSR (by address) to the feature gate that enables it. Addresses
56	// are the HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST scalars plus the PMA block. A CSR with no
57	// custom-extension gate is ALWAYS (a base machine CSR every Andes core has).
58	// Maintainer note: a CSR added to HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST that needs gating must
59	// get a case here, else it defaults to ALWAYS (transported unconditionally).
60	constexpr AndesGate andes_gate_for(uint16_t csr_addr)
61	{
62	  switch (csr_addr) {
63	    case 0x801: return AndesGate::DSP;           // ucode (DSP overflow flag)
64	    case 0x800: return AndesGate::CODENSE;        // uitb  (CoDense table base)
65	    // jvt is Zcmt's table-jump base, NOT part of classic CoDense (exec.it +
66	    // uitb): a CoDense core without Zcmt faults a csrr of it (seen on
67	    // ax45mpv_premium, where it aborted the drain CSR sweep).
68	    case 0x017: return AndesGate::ZCMT;           // jvt   (Zcmt only)
69	    case 0x7C5: return AndesGate::POWERBRAKE;     // mpft_ctl
70	    case 0x7C2: return AndesGate::ECC;            // mecc_code
71	    case 0x7C6:                                   // mhsp_ctl
72	    case 0x7C7:                                   // msp_bound
73	    case 0x7C8: return AndesGate::STACKSAFE;      // msp_base
74	    case 0x7C0: return AndesGate::ILM;            // milmb (ILM base)
75	    case 0x7C1: return AndesGate::DLM;            // mdlmb (DLM base)
76	    // v4 M-ext CSR gates (HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST).
77	    // The counter-mask trio mcountermask_m (0x7D1), mcountermask_u (0x7D3),
78	    // mcounterwen (0x7CE) needs user mode (spec existence: PMNDS & misa[20]);
79	    // an M-only core does not implement them (a PB csrr faults cmderr=3,
80	    // aborting a CSR sweep), so gate them UMODE -- not PERF_MONITOR.
81	    case 0x30A: case 0x306: case 0x7D3:           // menvcfg, mcounteren, mcountermask_u
82	    case 0x7CE: case 0x7D1:                       // mcounterwen, mcountermask_m
83	    case 0x808: case 0x80B: case 0x811: case 0x813:  // uzobctl, ucctlbeginaddr, sleepvalue, umisc_ctl
84	      return AndesGate::UMODE;
85	    case 0x7D2: case 0x7D5: return AndesGate::SMODE;  // mcountermask_s, mslideleg
86	    case 0x747: return AndesGate::EPMP;           // mseccfg
87	    case 0x320: case 0xB03: case 0xB04: case 0xB05: case 0xB06:  // mcountinhibit, mhpmcounter3-6
88	    case 0x323: case 0x324: case 0x325: case 0x326:              // mhpmevent3-6
89	    case 0x7CF:                                                  // mcounterinten (PMNDS only)
90	      return AndesGate::PERF_MONITOR;
91	    case 0x740: case 0x741: case 0x742: case 0x744:  // mnscratch, mnepc, mncause, mnstatus
92	    case 0x7C3: case 0x7DE:                           // mnvec, mrnxvec
93	      return AndesGate::SMRNMI;
94	    case 0x7C9: return AndesGate::ALWAYS;         // mdcause (base Andes trap CSR)
95	    case 0x7D6: case 0x7D7: case 0x7D8: case 0x7D9:  // msavestatus, msaveepc1, msavecause1, msaveepc2
96	    case 0x7DA: case 0x7DB: case 0x7DC:              // msavecause2, msavedcause1, msavedcause2
97	      return AndesGate::EXCSLVL;
98	    case 0x307: case 0x347: case 0x7EC:           // mtvt, mintthresh, mcirq_entry
99	      return AndesGate::CLIC;
100	    case 0x30C: case 0x30D: case 0x30E: case 0x30F:  // mstateen0..3
101	      return AndesGate::SMSTATEEN;
102	    case 0x7CB: case 0x7CD: return AndesGate::CCTL;  // mcctlbeginaddr, mcctldata
103	    case 0x7F0: return AndesGate::PPI;            // mppib
104	    case 0x7F1: return AndesGate::FIO;            // mfiob
105	    case 0x7A0: case 0x7A1: case 0x7A2: case 0x7A5: case 0x7A8:  // tselect, tdata1, tdata2, tcontrol, mcontext
106	      return AndesGate::TRIGGER;
107	    default:
108	      // PMA cfg (0xBC0, 0xBC2) and addr (0xBD0..0xBDF) blocks.
109	      if (csr_addr == HYBRID_PMA_CFG0_CSR || csr_addr == HYBRID_PMA_CFG0_CSR + 2)
110	        return AndesGate::PMA;
111	      if (csr_addr >= HYBRID_PMA_ADDR0_CSR &&
112	          csr_addr < HYBRID_PMA_ADDR0_CSR + HYBRID_PMA_ADDR_NUM)
113	        return AndesGate::PMA;
114	      return AndesGate::ALWAYS;                    // mxstatus 0x7C4, mclk_ctl 0x7DF
115	  }
116	}
117	
118	// The set of Andes feature gates a target core has on. Built from the core's
119	// compiled-in config (config.inc) in the sim binary and injected into the
120	// resume/drain loops, so they transport only the CSRs the core implements.
121	// Default = every gate on (all(): no gating, the prior unconditional behavior).
122	struct AndesCaps {
123	  uint32_t gate_mask = ~0u;
124	
125	  static constexpr AndesCaps all()  { return AndesCaps{~0u}; }
126	  static constexpr AndesCaps none() { return AndesCaps{0u}; }
127	
128	  constexpr void set(AndesGate g, bool on = true)
129	  {
130	    const uint32_t bit = 1u << static_cast<unsigned>(g);
131	    if (on) gate_mask |= bit;
132	    else    gate_mask &= ~bit;
133	  }
134	
135	  constexpr bool gate_on(AndesGate g) const
136	  {
137	    return (gate_mask >> static_cast<unsigned>(g)) & 1u;
138	  }
139	
140	  // ALWAYS-gated CSRs are present on every core regardless of the mask.
141	  constexpr bool supports_csr(uint16_t csr_addr) const
142	  {
143	    const AndesGate g = andes_gate_for(csr_addr);
144	    return g == AndesGate::ALWAYS || gate_on(g);
145	  }
146	};
147	
148	// The gated CSR names this core supports, for the --describe card. Iterates the
149	// two single-source-of-truth X-macro lists: the v3 Andes custom CSRs and the v4
150	// M-ext CSRs. The driver uses this list to gate --verify, so a CSR the core
151	// lacks is neither restored, drained, nor compared.
152	inline std::vector<std::string> supported_andes_csr_names(const AndesCaps& caps)
153	{
154	  std::vector<std::string> out;
155	#define X(field, addr, name) if (caps.supports_csr(addr)) out.push_back(name);
156	  HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST(X)
157	#undef X
158	  // PMA group markers (whole pmacfg[]/pmaaddr[] blocks share one gate), so a
159	  // consumer can include/exclude PMA without listing all 18 entries.
160	  if (caps.supports_csr(HYBRID_PMA_CFG0_CSR))  out.push_back("pmacfg");
161	  if (caps.supports_csr(HYBRID_PMA_ADDR0_CSR)) out.push_back("pmaaddr");
162	  // v4 M-ext CSRs share the same address->gate map and --describe list.
163	#define X(field, addr, name) if (caps.supports_csr(addr)) out.push_back(name);
164	  HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST(X)
165	#undef X
166	  return out;
167	}
168	
169	}  // namespace hybrid
170	
171	#endif  // ANDES_HYBRID_ANDES_CAPS_HPP

possible to set triggers natively to ﬁre in M mode as well. In that case there is no higher privilege
mode to trap to. When such a trigger causes a breakpoint exception while already in a trap handler,

that it only disables triggers during the trap handler.
